model.what: the model's own forecast (data/congress/REPORT.md section 2), fitted on earlier cycles only, from what was known before the election (the orchestrator, 2026-11-07 05:58); no polls are used, so it carries less than forecasters then knew

calibration.note: k = the root mean square of z = (y - mean) / sd over these earlier years' races, each year forecast from its own earlier cycles

model.mean_is: 1/2 + national_forecast + b_lean * lean + b_inc * incumbency + b_lag * (last governor race's Democratic share - 1/2)
model.sd_is: sqrt(national_sd^2 + s_e^2); national_sd = k s_a sqrt(1 + z (Z'Z)^-1 z'), s_e = k s_e_fitted, z = (1, midterm * P, (1 - midterm) * P), P = +1 Democratic president, -1 Republican; k the calibration factor

variant.note: the mean as fitted, normal tails first (no variant of round 5 passed its test for this level; REPORT 2.7)

near_tie.note: not adopted for this level: on the years it reaches it does not both raise the log score and bring the near-even count nearer (REPORT 2.6)

p.not_computed: no earlier governor race in MO that a Democrat and a Republican led is in Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder (from 2006) or Algara and Amlani (before 2006); Algara and Amlani's Missouri rows fall short of Missouri's official returns, which equal Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder's totals, by 7% for the Democrat and 2% for the Republican in each of 2008, 2012 and 2016; in 2016 the shortfall is Kansas City's own rows to the vote (Koster 98,336, Greitens 25,284), since Kansas City reports apart from Jackson County [measured: pipeline/governor_counts.py]; the count is taken as incomplete; no published forecast for the race is reachable

forecast_inputs.last_governor_race_missing: no earlier governor race in MO that a Democrat and a Republican led is in Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder (from 2006) or Algara and Amlani (before 2006); Algara and Amlani's Missouri rows fall short of Missouri's official returns, which equal Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder's totals, by 7% for the Democrat and 2% for the Republican in each of 2008, 2012 and 2016; in 2016 the shortfall is Kansas City's own rows to the vote (Koster 98,336, Greitens 25,284), since Kansas City reports apart from Jackson County [measured: pipeline/governor_counts.py]; the count is taken as incomplete

notes: governors' totals here leave out candidates under ten votes, blank, over- and under-votes (the dataset's guide)

the count (pipeline/governor_counts.py): Missouri's official returns (Official Election Returns ... As announced by the Board of State Canvassers on Tuesday, December 02, 2008; https://www.sos.mo.gov/CMSImages/ElectionResultsStatistics/AllRacesGeneralNovember2008.pdf, read 2026-11-13T05:29:14Z) give the Democrat 1,680,611 and the Republican 1,136,364, this record's figures to the vote; Algara and Amlani's county returns give 1,560,588 and 1,110,048 [measured], short by 120,023 and 26,316 (the state's file gives no rows by county; in 2016 the shortfall is Kansas City's own rows to the vote). So the record's count stands with the state's (the orchestrator, 2026-11-13 05:26: "one each to ... Missouri (2008, 2012, 2016) ... for the state's certified governor count"; data/local/REPORT.md section 35)

notes: the count (pipeline/governor_counts.py): the candidates' votes are the Utah Lieutenant Governor's results of the 2008 general (the workbook its historical results page links as '2008 General', its Governor sheet's Total row): Huntsman 734,049, Springmeyer 186,503, Schanze 24,820 and the write-in Doughton's 153. The workbook bears no certified or official mark; Algara and Amlani's county returns give Huntsman 734,049 and Springmeyer 186,503, the state's figures to the vote, against Cha, Kuriwaki and Snyder's 700,565 and 175,301 [measured]. Two independent counts that agree by candidate stand against one (the orchestrator, 2026-11-13 05:15 (3) and 05:26: "Then the two-witness rule of 05:15 applies wherever it fits"); n and each p follow them, and so do D2's fits of later years and the last-governor-race inputs that read 2008 (data/local/REPORT.md section 35)
